label: UNCALIBRATED LIVE-MODEL EXPLORATORY SIMULATION
question: Will the following outcome occur before the cutoff? Peter Thiel explicitly agrees to a 20-minute call with Beckett Zahedi.
context:
Beckett Zahedi is 17 and is starting Princeton in fall 2026. He is building Aurelius, a supervisory optimization system for GPU fleets. In replay tests covering approximately 1.5 million public production requests, it produced approximately 724% more SLA-safe goodput per dollar. This has not been validated in a live production deployment and must not be represented as production-proven. Beckett has never contacted Peter Thiel and has no known mutual introduction. Beckett wants criticism and a short technical conversation, not an immediate investment. Peter Thiel is publicly known as a Founders Fund partner, a cofounder of PayPal and Palantir, and the founder of the Thiel Fellowship. Do not invent private beliefs, inbox behavior, scheduling details, or personal preferences for Peter.

Modelling scope for this simulation: model exactly two actors, the sender and the recipient named in the context above. Do not add assistants, colleagues, partners, or intermediaries. Do not assign the recipient any private beliefs, inbox habits, calendar state, screening rules, or personal preferences: nothing of that kind is known, and inventing it would make the simulation a story rather than a test.

decision_problem_payload_supplied.success_criteria: Success occurs only if a committed event authored by Peter Thiel's own actor contains an explicit agreement to speak with Beckett, an explicit acceptance of a 20-minute call, or a direct instruction to schedule the call. A generic acknowledgment, an assistant response, the Game Master's narration, message delivery, message opening, or inferred interest does not count as success.
constraints: The email must contain between 45 and 85 words excluding the subject line.
It must accurately describe the 724% result as a replay result, not production validation.
It must not claim a mutual connection or prior relationship.
It must make one clear request for a 20-minute call.
It must not ask Peter Thiel to invest.
It must not use false urgency, invented scarcity, or manipulative pressure.
It may offer a one-page technical memo.
Only public professional information and user-supplied information may be used.

Subject: 7.24× more useful work per GPU dollar

Peter—

I'm Beckett, 17, starting Princeton this fall. I built a supervisory optimizer for GPU fleets that produced 7.24× more SLA-safe goodput per dollar across 1.5M replayed production requests. It is not production-validated yet, but the mechanism is concrete. Would you be open to a 20-minute call next week? I can send a one-page technical memo first.

Subject: Where does this AI infrastructure thesis break?

Peter—

I think AI infrastructure is optimizing the wrong layer: individual schedulers make locally sensible choices while fleet-wide sequencing destroys goodput per dollar. I built a supervisory simulator that improved SLA-safe goodput/$ by 724% across 1.5M replayed requests. I'm 17 and starting Princeton this fall. Could I show you the result for 20 minutes and get your sharpest objection?

Subject: A contrarian infrastructure result from a 17-year-old

Peter—

Your work has pushed young builders to test unusual ideas before credentials arrive. I'm 17 and built an AI infrastructure optimizer that increased SLA-safe goodput per dollar by 724% in replay tests across 1.5M requests. I'm not asking you to invest. I want to know whether the thesis survives scrutiny. Would you take a 20-minute call next week?
